verdict: Better than r2 (5.19) but still not a fern plate. The wide is a believable one-point Kowloon canyon at night, and its title slot is clean against C30. `dawn` is the best frame: a woman at a shop window with real carriers in her hands. Four problems hold the stage back. First, `company` still reads as two men escorting Dawn, not as people she trusted. Second, the shop satchel in `window` is the same model as the black gift satchel, in dark charcoal leather one shade lighter than the gift. Only its gold hardware tells the two apart. Third, across the stage the signs are flat UI rectangles, most shop fronts are cold white and empty, and the street is thinly peopled, so the 'nine days of sightseeing' beat reads as a deserted late night. Fourth, the hands are still blocks or mittens, and Dawn's legs change between two consecutive shots: dark stockings in `dawn` (18-23), pale stone in `company` (shins about 53-65). The cause is the lights linked to her legs in `company`, not the tights mask. There are also three small sign overlaps near the vanishing point, and wires drawn across sign faces in `company`, that read as glyphs. Mean 5.44, lowest score cast at 4.5.
answers:
I checked the frames against d9fa391. All four graded JPEGs and raw PNGs in the working tree are byte-identical to that commit, and the stage code has not changed since. All values below are Rec.709 luma on the graded 1280x720 frames unless I say otherwise.

1. WIDE: THE EYE'S PATH TO DAWN. It mostly works but is not clean.
- Dawn sits close to the lower-right third point (x 826-852, y 500-585). Her pale head is the hottest small point in that area (max 172).
- She stands on the brightest stretch of her pavement: median about 48-52 by her, about 42 farther along. That gap is much smaller than the 68 against 39 reported at a881741.
- The two signs hanging over her stretch are the brightest large shapes in the frame: yellow (688-770, 296-378) median 99 and teal (803-856, 270-370) median 102. They sit on the diagonal above her and do pull the eye down toward her.
- The eye reaches the upper-left first, though. The big near panels there are the largest areas: beige 255-385 x 45-135 (median 66), tall white 338-383 x 200-320 (median 81), red (median 48), and the tall tan panel at 62-150 cut by the top edge (median 61). The teal road reflection (640-700, 560-700, p95 118) and the rails then pull the eye to the vanishing point, not to Dawn.
- Near Dawn, T1 stands frontal at about x 778, y 502-556, next to a warm tan lightbox. His walk_up already has a full stride in the code (legs_walk at 17-21 / 11-14 degrees), but seen head-on he reads as standing still. His pale head (max 160) competes with hers.
- Her dark suit (median about 42-46) barely separates from the lit pier on her left (about 50). It does separate from the dark doorway on her right (21-33).
- Net: you find her in about 1.5 s, not at once.

2. DAWN: CARRIER GRIPS AND PAVEMENT.
- The grips are now physically right. Both sets of handles converge into the hands. The kraft bag's two cords loop up into the right hand, and the tissue bag's cords go into the left fist. The r2 gap is gone.
- The hands themselves still fail. The right hand is a pale rectangular block with no fingers (median about 60-68, p95 about 110-113), the brightest skin after the head. It reads as a cuff or a stump. The left hand is a closed grey mitten. The fingers are already curled 75-88 degrees round the cords (CURL_GRIP), so the problem is the value and the angle of the fist, not too little curl.
- The bun is built on the head's midline at the back of the skull (cast.py). From this rear three-quarter (the camera is about 128 degrees off her facing), the back of the skull is the screen-left edge of the head, so the bun breaks that silhouette at ear height. It can read as a lump on the side of the head rather than a low bun at the nape.
- Pavement: the coloured joint glints from r2 are fixed. Off the reflection the joints are neutral and dark (chroma median about 2-5).
- Two pavement faults remain. (a) The teal sign reflection is confined to exactly one file of slabs, with hard edges at the joints on both sides (chroma about 13-22). It holds the frame's highest-chroma pixel and looks like a lit runway lane, not water. The cause is in pavers(): the border roughness (0.60) is applied after the wet mix, so it overrides the wet zones at every joint. (b) The per-slab random value (about 25 against 41 on neighbouring tiles along row 650) reads as a checker texture, not relaid stone.
- The shop window she is looking into is almost black. Its shelf bags have median 27-28, so the 'lit shop window' does not throw light on her.

3. WINDOW: REFLECTED FACE.
- The face is there and survives the grade: median 25.1 against 19.1 on the felt to its left and 13.1 to its right. That is about 1.3x against the adjacent felt, a little lower than the reported 25.2 over 13.9. It should survive the encode.
- It reads as a faceless ghost standing inside the shop between the hobo and the satchel, not as a reflection on glass.
- The only glass cue is the thin dark pane-joint bead at the right edge (x about 1248-1256), and it reads as a frame line. There is no street colour and no sheen on the glass.

4. WINDOW: SHELF COLOURS.
- The slate tote passes: graded median 33, hue 215, saturation 0.28. It is clearly slate blue.
- The olive hobo is borderline. It reads as dark green-grey, with graded saturation 0.08-0.12.
- The 'stone' satchel fails. Its dye runs from (0.066, 0.059, 0.046) to (0.162, 0.150, 0.126) with the scan's own tone, and the dark scan keeps it near the low end. Graded, it has median 33 and saturation 0.06-0.09: neutral charcoal, not warm stone.
- It is the same satchel model as the gift. That is by design: COVERAGE row 353 has the shelf echo the evidence bags and differ only in colour. So the colour has to carry the difference. On screen it reads as the black gift satchel one shade lighter, which breaks the intent of C30 (no black) even though its value is technically 'a little above' the felt.
- The one thing that already sets it apart is the gold clasp. The gift satchel in evidence_table/purses has pale steel-grey fittings.
- The whole display is underlit. Median 22.6 and p99 60, with only faint pools under the three spots, so the 'lit shelf' does not read.
- The left-quarter grey slab from r2 is now darker (33 graded) but is still a flat, featureless block.

5. COMPANY: DO THEY READ AS WALKING TOGETHER? Not yet.
- The strides now differ, the hands are empty and the suits differ (left man median 42.7, right man 21.9). That fixes the 'clones in step' part of r2.
- The formation is essentially unchanged: Dawn in the middle, a man on each side, about 1.0 m centre to centre from each (0.7 m sideways).
- The code already turns the Organiser's head 12 degrees toward her and hers 7 degrees toward him. From directly behind, neither turn reads, so all three heads look square ahead.
- Two men flanking a woman from behind reads as an escort. COVERAGE row 9 ('people she trusted', beside two men, no faces, no gesture) needs closeness or shared attention, and that is possible without faces or gesture.
- The near-left man (T1) has his right shoe running off the bottom edge of the frame (x 456-490, down to row 719).
- Dawn's legs read as bare pale stone here (shins about 53-65; Codex reported 53.1 and 58.5) but as dark stockings in `dawn` (18-23). That is a continuity jump between two consecutive shots.
- In the wide her near calf already reads pale too (about 63 against 32 on the far calf).
- The tights mask is not the cause: legmask comes from vertex weights, which do not change with the pose. The lift comes from the lights linked to her body in this beat: 'left pavement return' (added at bb1cc82 to keep the stockings readable) and 'boutique door spill' at a 0.26 trim.

6. SIGN OVERLAPS THAT READ AS GLYPHS. I am flagging these:
- (a) Wide (646-671, 388-410): two tan panels overlap into a stepped inverted-L / Γ.
- (b) Wide (583-600, 470-497): a teal vertical panel partly covered by something dark, so only a teal bracket '[' or 'コ' outline remains, with a small teal square beside it. This is end_building()'s teal 2.4 x 6.5 panel at a=26, which projects to about (591-600, 472-498). end_building() is not checked by separated_sign().
- (c) Wide (614-636, 474-481): two tan bars butted into a step. This is minor.
- (d) Company: a wire runs exactly horizontal across the violet panel at about (313-357, 62), drawing a '一' stroke on it. A kinked wire crosses the lower part of the small tan panel above the teal one at about (523-547, 103-117), drawing a check-mark stroke.
- (e) Dawn and company: the teal panel has two or three wires crossing its face, and a cream bar butts against its lower-left corner, making a stepped compound shape. This is the weakest of the flags.
- The satchel's twisted gold lock in `window` is a borderline letter-like squiggle at 2x. Recheck it after the re-light.

7. TITLE SLOT AGAINST C30. It passes.
- Box x 450-830, y 40-230 on the graded wide: median 12.1, mean 13.5, p99 28.1, max 39.0. That agrees with Codex's 12.3, 28.6, 40.1.
- Every pixel above 30 sits at y 133-229, almost all at x 730-820 (the right facade's balcony edges), plus a few at about 610 (the wire) and 450-456.
- No sign face or bright window is inside the box.
- The violet/burgundy sign at the top edge now starts at about x 872, clear of 830.
- Nits: one straight vertical hanging wire at x 609-614 brightens from 13 at y 50 to about 29-32 by y 200 and runs through where the G of HONG will fall. C30 allows one or two thin wires across the box, so this is optional. A faint dark '+' at about (575-650, 135) is harmless at real brightness.
- The 'night sky' is really a dark far facade (a contrast stretch shows its structure), so nothing would show as sky.
- The title's right end (about x 755) will overlap the facade edge lines at 730-760, which is acceptable.

fixes.problem: The formation reads as a custody escort. Dawn is centred, with a man on each side about 1.0 m away. The existing head turns (Organiser 12 degrees, Dawn 7 degrees) do not read from behind, so all three heads look square ahead. T1's right shoe runs off the bottom frame edge.
fixes.fix: In BLOCK['company'], stop flanking her. Make Dawn and the Organiser a loose pair with Dawn on the kerb side: Dawn (5.55, 16.6), Organiser (6.12, 16.75). That is about 0.55-0.6 m centre to centre at the same pace; check that the swinging arms clear. Put T1 half a step ahead on the shop side, e.g. (6.55, 17.4), not behind her left. In act(), raise the company glance from 12 / -7 to about 20-25 degrees for the Organiser and 10-12 for Dawn, within solve_head's limits. Turn T1's head 15-20 degrees toward the boutique glass. Looking is not gesture, so COVERAGE row 9 holds. With these marks the nearest feet project at about y 620, well clear of the bottom edge. Keep every foot at least 25 px above it.

fixes.problem: The 'warm stone' satchel stays near its dark dye end (0.066, 0.059, 0.046) and grades to median 33 at saturation 0.06-0.09. That is a charcoal satchel of the same model as the black gift. The display is underlit (median 22.6, p99 60), with only faint pools under the spots.
fixes.fix: In boutique() dyes, lift handbag-satchel from (0.066, 0.059, 0.046) / (0.162, 0.150, 0.126) to a true warm stone, about (0.20, 0.185, 0.16) / (0.34, 0.32, 0.28). Keep its gold hardware. The gift satchel in evidence_table/purses has pale steel-grey fittings, so gold is the one thing that already sets the shop bag apart; gunmetal would bring it closer to the gift. Raise bq_spot_tote/satchel/shoulder from 145-150 W to about 280 W, with size 14 and blend 0.2, so each bag sits in a visible pool on the felt. Then rebalance so the felt reads about 35 graded and the bags 40-50. That keeps C30's 'at the felt's value or a little above' at a visible level. Check that the tote stays slate blue (hue 200-220) and the hobo reads olive (graded saturation 0.12 or more).

fixes.problem: Dawn's legs read as bare pale stone here (shins about 53-65) but as dark stockings in `dawn` (18-23), a continuity jump between consecutive shots. In the wide her near calf also reads pale (about 63 against 32).
fixes.fix: Leave tights() alone. legmask comes from vertex-group weights, which do not change with the pose, and it works in `dawn`. The lift is from lights linked to her body. In `company` these are 'left pavement return' (added at bb1cc82 to keep the stockings readable) and 'boutique door spill' at a 0.26 trim. Keep the separating edge but not a lit calf: cut 'left pavement return' to about a quarter of its energy, or narrow it to a rim on the trailing calf. Drop the door-spill trim to about 0.12. Stop when the shins read about 25-30 graded, under her skirt (about 32 here). In the wide the untrimmed door spill (142 W, aimed at her hip) does the same to her near calf. Trim it there, or flag her legs with a shadow-only card below the skirt that keeps the light on the bags, so all three shots agree.

fixes.problem: Three sign overlaps read as glyphs: a stepped tan Γ at (646-671, 388-410), a teal '[' bracket at (583-600, 470-497), and butted tan bars at (614-636, 474-481).
fixes.fix: In separated_sign(), reject any projected overlap (overlap > 0), and any two rectangles within 0.01 NDC of each other when both are lit, instead of the current 0.15*min(size, area0) allowance. Run the same check for end_building()'s four panels against the street signs. The '[' is its teal 2.4 x 6.5 panel at a=26, which projects to about (591-600, 472-498), with something dark covering its middle. After the change, render a sign-ID or flat-emission pass of the wide. Check every compound silhouette under 40 px by eye, and recheck the C30 title box.

fixes.problem: Wires drawn across sign faces read as strokes. A horizontal wire across the violet panel at about (313-357, 62) reads as '一'. A kinked wire over the tan panel at about (523-547, 103-117) reads as a check mark. The dawn camera has the same wires over the teal panel.
fixes.fix: wires() keeps cables clear of signs only in 3D, by y and height. Add a screen-space check: project each span into the company and dawn cameras, and move or re-sag any span whose screen path crosses a lit sign face. For example, shift its y by 0.6 m or change the sag so it passes above or below the panel. Never let a wire run parallel to a panel's top or bottom edge across its face.

fixes.problem: The hands read as a pale block (right: median about 60-68, p95 about 110-113, the brightest skin after the head) and a mitten (left). The midline bun breaks the back silhouette at ear height and can read as a lump on the side of the head. The window she faces is dark (shelf bags median 27-28), so the 'lit shop window' does not light her.
fixes.fix: The fingers are already closed round the cords (CURL_GRIP: 75-88 degrees, thumb 35-40), so more curl will not help. Lower Dawn's hands_stone from 0.36 to about 0.30 so the hands sit under the face. Pronate the right wrist about 20-30 degrees so the knuckle line and the separate thumb face the lens instead of the flat edge of the hand. The bun is already centred at the back of the skull (cast.py), so do not move it sideways. In dawn(), lower it another 2-3 cm and pull it about 1 cm closer to the skull, so from this rear three-quarter it sits at the nape below the ear line. For the window: 'display shelf return' reaches only her suit and the carried bags. bq_glow already runs at its full 60 W in this camera, and it already brightens her right hand, so neither light lifts the shelf. The shelf bags are lit by bq_spot_* and bq_top, so the spot raise in the window fix will lift them here too; check that they reach about 40 graded. For a warm edge on the right side of her suit, raise TRIMS['dawn']['display shelf return'] from 12/28 to about 0.8.

fixes.problem: The teal reflection is confined to one file of slabs, with hard edges at the joints (chroma about 13-22), and reads as a lit runway lane. The per-slab random value (about 25 against 41) reads as a checker texture.
fixes.fix: In pavers(), the border roughness step (_fmix(border, r, 0.60)) comes after the wet mix and overrides it at every joint. Apply it before the wet and damp mixes, so reflections cross the joints in wet patches. Rotate or stretch the wetf noise (scale 0.7) so wet patches span 2-4 slabs irregularly. Narrow the slab tone range from (0.048-0.086) to about (0.058-0.078), and leave the 'odd' relaid slabs as they are. If needed, cut the 'sign spill' area lights of the boosted side>0 signs at y 17-22 by about 40%.

fixes.problem: The eye path competes. The big near-left panels (beige median 66, tall white 81) pull against Dawn, and so does T1, frontal with a pale head beside a tan lightbox at about x 778. The stage brief asks for fronts 'burning fluorescent or warm, spilling onto the wet pavement', but most fronts near her are cold white and empty.
fixes.fix: For side<0 signs nearest the camera (yw < 14), cap strength at 0.35 so they recede. T1's walk_up already has a full stride (legs_walk at 17-21 / 11-14 degrees), but head-on it does not show. Move him to the far-left pavement, or put him on a diagonal path so his stride reads in three-quarter, so that Dawn's is the only pale head in the right half. Update KEEP if his mark moves. The shop lights are set in shop(); spill_out() only places goods. In shop(), send the 3-4 lit units nearest Dawn (y 12-30) down the existing warm branch, colour (1.0, 0.8, 0.58), so their spill_ and fill_ lights lay warm pools on the pavement under the walkers, against the cool signs.

fixes.problem: The street is thinly peopled: seven walkers on the pavements, plus two shopkeepers inside shops. The clutter from dressing() (crates, cartons, bollards) sits in the dark or far off. So 'nine days of sightseeing and shopping' reads as a deserted late night.
fixes.fix: Add 6-8 more walkers in pairs and threes on both pavements at y 20-45, built from varied people.man and woman() variants. apply_camera() already drops subdivision for distant figures. Extend dressing() with a few pieces where shop light catches them, such as a bin, a folded A-frame stand with a blank face and a parked delivery trolley. Keep them off the KEEP marks and out of the title box.

fixes.problem: The reflected face reads as a ghost standing inside the shop. The only glass cue is the thin dark pane-joint bead at the right edge (x about 1248-1256), which reads as a frame line.
fixes.fix: Raise glass_refl in the window camera from 0.017 to about 0.028. Signboards are still visible to glossy rays in this camera, so a faint vertical streak of one sign colour and the street's pale fascia line will reflect at the top-left. The glass already carries the 'glass smudges' roughness noise (0.025-0.06 in this camera, scale 7). Widen that range, or add a finer dust noise (scale about 40), so the sheen breaks up. Keep the face at about 1.3-1.5x the felt beside it, and recheck that ratio after the spot raise in the satchel fix.

fixes.problem: A straight vertical wire at x 609-614 (luma 13 to about 30) runs through where the title's G will sit. C30 allows thin wires across the box, so this is a nit. The far canyon shows denoiser smears at 64 samples (the raw PNG records 64). A tall tan panel (62-150, 0-240) and the burgundy panel are cut by the top edge.
fixes.fix: If convenient, move that hanging wire to x < 520 on screen or give it a diagonal run. Render the wide final at 128 samples or more, or render at 2560 and downscale, to remove the painterly smears around (560-720, 330-520). Shorten or lower the top-left tall panel so it clears the top edge by at least 10 px.
